title: Zero detection for a single colimit-site inverse-image unit
statement: Let J be a small filtered category, F : J → Cat a diagram of small categories, and P_j precoverages satisfying the site axioms and finite covering condition of [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-of-sites]. Suppose the transition functors preserve coverings and covering pullbacks, are continuous, and have set-valued inverse image preserving finite limits and finite colimits. Let V be a cocone with object and arrow colimit witnesses [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let Q be a precoverage on V.pt satisfying the same site axioms, with covering presieves exactly the images of stage coverings. Suppose the canonical stage functors preserve coverings and covering pullbacks, are continuous, and have set-valued inverse image preserving finite limits and finite colimits. Fix j, an abelian sheaf G on P_j [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], X in F_j, and z in G(X). If the canonical unit G(X) → (V_j^*G)(V_j X) sends z to zero, then there are k and d : j → k such that the canonical unit G(X) → (F_d^*G)(F_d X) sends z to zero. There is no coefficient system or outer colimit in this statement.

proof.text: The object and arrow colimit witnesses identify the supplied V with the constructed filtered colimit category. The characterization hQ of image coverings identifies the topology. Transport the inverse-image section formula of 0A35 across this equivalence, identifying the unit by uniqueness of left adjoints.

Represent z and zero at the identity stage through its inverse-image unit, an isomorphism. Apply the same-stage equality clause of lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise to the underlying-set colimit over Under j. It gives one arrow from the identity presentation, hence d : j → k, killing the representative. The transition unit equation identifies this image with the unit along d on z. Abelian filtered colimits are computed on underlying sets; additive endpoint transports preserve zero.
